court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma

issues.label: Standard for child support above guidelines
issues.why: Father's income exceeds the $15,000 guideline maximum, requiring the court to determine how to set support beyond the schedule.

issues.label: Basis for $2,250 award
issues.why: Court based the award on Father's volunteered offer rather than statutory factors or the children's needs.

issues.label: Departure from Archer v. Archer
issues.why: Court expressly declined to follow Archer, so its correctness in doing so must be reviewed.

issues.label: Children's actual expenses and needs
issues.why: Court must weigh evidence of the children's direct and indirect living expenses in setting support above guidelines.

issues.label: Best interests of the children
issues.why: Support determinations must serve the children's best interests and standard of living.

issues.label: Credibility of Father's expense estimate
issues.why: Father lacked personal knowledge of children's expenses, affecting the weight of his testimony.

issues.label: Whether ruling against weight of evidence
issues.why: The abuse-of-discretion standard requires assessing if the award is clearly against the evidence.

issues.label: Failure to give notice of income increase
issues.why: Father violated the 2021 order's notice provision, relevant to modification and fees.

issues.label: Retroactivity/effective date of modification
issues.why: Court must consider from what date the increased support applies given Father's rising income.

issues.label: Statutory authority for attorney fees
issues.why: Fees require a specific statute or agreement, so the authority basis must be identified.

issues.label: Ability to pay disparity
issues.why: Relative financial resources of the parties bear on the equity of fee awards.

issues.label: Reasonableness of fee amount
issues.why: Court found requested fees reasonable but awarded only a portion, requiring scrutiny.

issues.label: Partial fee award justification
issues.why: Court limited fees to discovery efforts without elaborating, raising adequacy-of-findings concerns.

issues.label: Effect of Father's litigation conduct
issues.why: Father's delays and attorney changes may justify broader fee shifting.

issues.label: Effect of Mother declining settlement offers
issues.why: Father argues Mother's rejection of offers should limit fees.

issues.label: Mother's earning capacity
issues.why: Father contends Mother could earn more by practicing law, relevant to support and fees.

issues.label: Registration of foreign paternity decree
issues.why: Jurisdiction and enforceability depend on proper registration of the Texas decree in Oklahoma.

issues.label: De novo review of legal questions
issues.why: Underlying legal questions within abuse-of-discretion review must be reviewed independently.

issues.label: Validity of self-executing modification provision
issues.why: The 2021 order allowed new guidelines without a new motion, raising procedural propriety.
